entities.name: Q3 2025 Performance Metrics
entities.description: Operational performance targets and achievements for Claims Operations in Q3 2025
entities.overview: Set of key performance indicators tracking claims processing efficiency, accuracy, and throughput. Shows 81.3% auto-adjudication rate against 85% target, 4.2 second average processing time, and 99.7% payment accuracy.
entities.details: Claims volume reached 2.4M (up 8% from Q2) split between Professional (2.0M), Institutional (350K), and Pharmacy (50K on legacy system). Auto-adjudication rate of 81.3% remains below 85% target due to incomplete rules migration from HealthLogic. Average processing time improved from 5.1 to 4.2 seconds due to synchronous fraud scoring. Denial rate of 12.4% with top reasons being member eligibility issues (3.2%), missing authorizations (2.8%), duplicates (2.1%), non-covered services (1.9%), and timely filing limits (1.4%). Payment accuracy at 99.7% with fraud holds affecting 0.05% of volume (1,247 claims).

relationships.reasoning: Auto-adjudication rate directly depends on rules engine performance
Fraud holds and processing time improvements from fraud detection optimization

entities.reasoning: Specific quantitative business rules and targets that govern system performance evaluation

entities.name: Capitation
entities.description: Per-member-per-month (PMPM) payment model for providers regardless of services rendered
entities.overview: Alternative payment model where providers receive fixed monthly payments per enrolled member rather than fee-for-service payments. Currently not supported by Clearview's Payment Engine but requested by larger provider groups in contract negotiations.
entities.details: Flat per-member-per-month (PMPM) payment structure that contrasts with Clearview's current fee-for-service only model. Large multi-specialty provider groups are requesting capitated contracts during negotiations. Implementation would require significant changes to the Payment Engine architecture. Provider Network team and larger provider groups have been advocating for this capability, leading to plans for a Q1 2026 design proposal to scope the effort.

entities.name: DRG Grouper
entities.description: System logic that assigns Diagnosis Related Group codes to institutional claims
entities.overview: Complex algorithmic logic that categorizes inpatient hospital stays into Diagnosis Related Groups (DRGs) for payment purposes. Represents some of the most complex rules in the migration from HealthLogic to the new rules engine.
entities.details: Sophisticated medical coding and payment logic that analyzes institutional claims (hospital inpatient stays) and assigns them to appropriate Diagnosis Related Group (DRG) categories. DRGs are used to determine payment amounts for hospital services based on diagnosis, procedures, patient characteristics, and discharge status. The DRG grouper logic includes complex edge cases that are among the most challenging rules to migrate from the HealthLogic system to Clearview's new rules engine.

entities.name: Multi-Claim Bundling
entities.description: Logic for grouping related claims together for coordinated adjudication and payment
entities.overview: Complex business rules that identify and group related claims that should be processed together rather than independently. Part of the challenging rules being migrated from HealthLogic system.
entities.details: Sophisticated adjudication logic that identifies claims that should be grouped and processed together for accurate payment determination. This includes scenarios like multiple claims from the same episode of care, related surgical procedures, or claims that need coordinated benefit application. These bundling rules are among the complex logic being migrated from HealthLogic and contribute to the difficulty in achieving the 85% auto-adjudication target.

entities.name: Rules Engine Connectivity Incident (August 15)
entities.description: SEV-1 incident caused by VPN tunnel failure to HealthLogic data center affecting claims processing
entities.overview: 45-minute SEV-1 incident on August 15, 2025 when VPN tunnel to HealthLogic's data center failed, disrupting rules engine connectivity and claims processing. External issue that reinforces need to migrate away from HealthLogic.
entities.details: Severity-1 incident lasting 45 minutes on August 15, 2025 when the VPN tunnel between Clearview and HealthLogic's data center experienced a flap, causing connectivity issues with the Rules Engine. While the root cause was external to Clearview (HealthLogic's infrastructure issue), it disrupted claims processing and highlighted the dependency risk of using an external vendor system. This incident provides additional justification for the ongoing migration away from HealthLogic to an internal rules engine solution.

entities.overview: SEV-2 incident during Q3 2025 when MedConnect Exchange changed character encoding in institutional claim batches without notifying Clearview, causing processing failures.
entities.details: Severity-2 incident during Q3 2025 when MedConnect Exchange, one of Clearview's EDI clearinghouse partners, switched character sets in their EDI 837 Institutional claim batches without providing advance notification to Clearview. entities.overview: Two separate SEV-2 incidents during Q3 2025 when the accumulator reservation cleanup job failed due to conflicts with Cloud SQL maintenance windows. Indicates need for better job scheduling coordination.
entities.details: Two SEV-2 incidents occurred during Q3 2025 when the scheduled accumulator reservation cleanup job failed to execute properly due to timing conflicts with Cloud SQL database maintenance windows. These failures suggest inadequate coordination between scheduled maintenance and critical batch job timing.
